headline: Democrats vow oversight/impeachment, some Republicans call for lame-duck ouster, White House states full confidence
dek: Democrats vowed intense oversight of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, with some prepared to try to impeach him. Incoming House Armed Services Committee Chair Adam Smith pledged to investigate Hegseth, probing the Iran war, the purge of senior officers, and the commercial-messaging-app discussion of a…
sources: USA Today reporting of on-record statements by Rep. Jason Crow, Sen. Thom Tillis, Rep. Thomas Massie, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, incoming House Armed Services chair Adam Smit
fault_line: Accountability or partisan revenge — is the Hegseth impeachment drive a reckoning for an unpopular war, or a campaign promise being cashed in regardless of the war's outcome?

sections.what_happened: Democrats vowed intense oversight of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, with some prepared to try to impeach him. Incoming House Armed Services Committee Chair Adam Smith pledged to investigate Hegseth, probing the Iran war, the purge of senior officers, and the commercial-messaging-app discussion of a sensitive operation. Rep. Jason Crow said Nov 4: 'I'm going after Pete Hegseth. I'm going to be relentless night and day to get him out of the Pentagon.' Rep. Thomas Massie pledged to impeach Hegseth when lawmakers return next week and wrote on social media: 'Trump should fire Hegseth to avoid Hegseth's impeachment. It's the honorable thing to do.' Sen. Thom Tillis (R) told CBS News Nov 4: 'Pete Hegseth has a reckoning.' Some Republican lawmakers are calling for Hegseth's ouster during the lame-duck session. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said Trump 'has full confidence in Secretary Hegseth'; Parnell said Hegseth is '100% committed to leading the Department until the end of President Trump's term.' CONTEXT THAT LOWERS NOVELTY: Crow's ouster pledge is a restatement — he called removal 'priority No. 1' on CBS Face the Nation on Oct 28 (Military.com) and on CNN Oct 29; Massie's eight articles of impeachment date from September (blocked by House recess). The genuinely new Nov 4 elements are the Tillis 'reckoning' quote, the lame-duck GOP ouster calls, and the White House full-confidence statement.
sections.what_verified: USA Today has NO declared tier in the registry and therefore does NOT count toward corroboration. The pre-midterm pledges are independently documented (Military.com Oct 28 for Crow's 'priority No. 1'; Matzav/Newsmax Oct 26 for Jeffries/Crow/Massie pledges and the eight September articles), but those outlets likewise have no declared tier, so they are reported with attribution and do not raise the family count. The quotes are primary-source statements by their authors, relayed by USA Today.
sections.what_disputed: White House full confidence (Kelly) + Parnell '100% committed' + Trump's own Nov 4 'doing a very good job' directly contradict any reading that Hegseth's exit is decided. Procedurally, House impeachment needs only a simple majority but Senate conviction needs two-thirds — so even a successful House vote would very likely not remove him. Massie's September articles never reached a vote because of the House recess.
sections.why_matters: Update Short inside the proven Trump-Iran endgame lane, distinct from 0000-01 (which covered Trump's private deliberations): lead with the on-record Tillis 'reckoning' quote — a Republican senator, not a Democrat — then Crow's pledge and the White House full-confidence reply. Do not present impeachment as decided or removal as likely; name the Senate two-thirds bar on screen.
